extracted.intended_audience: OPQA reviewers / patent quality reviewers at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form fields for Office of Patent Quality Assurance (OPQA) reviewers to assess statutory and nonstatutory double patenting rejections, other rejections, and omitted rejections (35 U.S.C. 101, nonstatutory DP, 102, 103). Instructs how to record claim-identification, reasons for noncompliance, characteristics, feedback, and proposed omitted rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Were all 35 U.S.C. 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection(s) in compliance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 U.S.C. 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection(s) in compliance? Yes or No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection was made in the Office action being reviewed, the answer must be updated to either Yes or No. i. If 'Yes', go to question 7. ii. If 'No', continue to question 3. The determination of compliance is based on the rejection properly identifying the claim(s) and being supported by sufficient evidence to support the rejection of the claim(s). Consult the statutory compliance standard and scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claim(s) with non-compliant 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim discussed individually as a basis for the noncompliance in an 'Explanation of Noncompliance' section in addition to those dependent claims which inherit the noncompliance must be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in (check only one): a. Only the independent claim(s); b. Only the dependent claim(s); c. Both the independent claim(s) and dependent claim(s). This question is to identify the type of claim which is the root of the noncompliance (where the basis is first introduced in the claim tree). Only one box may be selected. Examples illustrate how to choose a/b/c.

rubrics_metrics.name: For 101 noncompliant claims, was another compliant 101 statutory double patenting rejection applied?
rubrics_metrics.description: For all of the claims identified as noncompliant under question 3, was another compliant 35 USC 101 statutory double patenting rejection applied? Yes or No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual claim may be rejected under 101 Statutory Double Patenting under multiple bases with one basis being compliant while others are not compliant. If every claim listed as having a noncompliant 101 SDP rejection also has another compliant basis for the rejection, answer 'Yes'. If even one does not have a compliant prior art rejection against it, answer 'No'. Consult 'MRF In-part Instruction' document for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Noncompliance reason — Failure to properly identify claims/statute (5a)
rubrics_metrics.description: 5a: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When either the claim(s) or the statute is the basis of the noncompliance, this box should be checked. Do not use this box to capture when the reviewer believes the claims were improperly rejected on the merits (use 5b for insufficient evidence). If the examiner improperly made the rejection provisional instead of non-provisional (or vice versa), check 5a. Do not check 5a when the reviewer determines the rejection should have been made under Nonstatutory Double Patenting (raise as omitted instead). If additional claims should have been included in the grounds of rejection, raise as an omitted 101 SDP rejection, not 5a.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Noncompliance reason — Insufficient evidence (5b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 5b: The rejection(s) does not provide sufficient evidence to support that the claimed invention is directed to the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 5b is checked, then the basis for lack of sufficient evidence must be identified by checking at least one of 5bi-5bii. Only comments directed to the basis for noncompliance based on lack of sufficient evidence should be included. The write up should avoid rhetorical questioning and should not be personalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Insufficient evidence subcriteria — no explanation (5bi)
rubrics_metrics.description: 5bi: The rejection(s) fails to provide any explanation supporting the claim(s) being of the same scope (e.g., limitation matching between claim sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If checked, the Explanation of noncompliance related to lack of sufficient evidence must describe the basis for lack of evidence. The reviewer should provide an explanation consistent with the box checked, avoid rhetorical questioning, and not personalize the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Insufficient evidence subcriteria — insufficient explanation (5bii)
rubrics_metrics.description: 5bii: The rejection(s) fails to provide a sufficient explanation supporting the claim(s) being of the same scope (e.g., limitation matching between claim sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanation of noncompliance related to lack of sufficient evidence consistent with boxes checked under 5b; the write up should be an assessment of the work product and avoid rhetorical questioning or personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Additional Information/Feedback — raise Nonstatutory DP (6a)
rubrics_metrics.description: 6a: The rejection(s) should have been made under Nonstatutory Double Patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correct basis for the rejection may be raised as an omitted Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Additional Information/Feedback — unreasonable claim interpretation (6b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 6b: The noncompliance is the result of an unreasonable claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 6b when the basis for noncompliance is based on a limitation which was improperly construed and/or given patent significance. Do not check 6b if the rejection provides no indication of how the claims are being interpreted. Only check when the rejection provides guidance/indication of interpretation that is unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Additional Information/Feedback — none of the above (6c)
rubrics_metrics.description: 6c: None of the above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 6c if neither 6a nor 6b apply. The reviewer should not guess about root cause; checked boxes should be supported by explanations in the noncompliance sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Comments field (suggestions, feedback, best practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional comments: suggestions, feedback, best practices that would benefit the examiner, but not directed to any basis of noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments here should not be directed to any basis of a noncompliance. Issues related to non-compliance should be provided in the appropriate comment boxes under Question 5. Providing suggestions, feedback and best practices is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection(s) — limited claim lumping
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) addresses substantially all claims individually and only groups claims together that are of substantially similar scope (i.e. limited claim lumping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These boxes represent characteristics that may be exemplified in rejections made under 35 U.S.C. 101 Statutory Double Patenting. The reviewer should check all boxes that apply to the office action reviewed. 'Substantially' and 'reasonably' permit reviewer judgment. Checking a characteristic does not reflect on accuracy/effectiveness — only indicates presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 — reasonably pinpoints where substantially all limitations are met
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) reasonably pinpoints where substantially all limitations are met by the conflicting claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection points to where claim limitations are met by the conflicting claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 — statements of patentable weight included
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of patentable weight are included, particularly when patentable weight is not being given to any of the following: Intended use limitations, Preamble, Claim language that suggests or makes optional some structure or steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate presence of patentable weight statements, especially when patentable weight is being denied for items like preamble or intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 — claim interpretation stated
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) sets forth a claim interpretation that points out how the examiner is interpreting the claim/term/phrase for purposes of the rejection(s) (e.g. BRI, special definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate when the office action shows the examiner's interpretation (broadest reasonable interpretation or special definition) used for the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 — detailed legal analysis included
rubrics_metrics.description: Included detailed legal analysis of applicable legal issues through a detailed analysis of the claim(s) and the case law/policy that applies thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the office action includes detailed legal analysis citing case law/policy and applies it to the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 — detailed technical analysis included
rubrics_metrics.description: Included detailed technical analysis in regards to the invention and/or the conflicting claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the office action includes detailed technical analysis applicable to the contested claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 — included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s) (not general FP language or indication of claims with allowable subject matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when action provides concrete suggestions to overcome the rejection (not generic or only pointing to allowable subject matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 101 — none of the above
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the above characteristics apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when none of the listed characteristics reasonably apply to the office action reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accolade for 101 rejections available?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to 101 Statutory Double Patenting Rejection(s)? Yes or No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any 101 SDP rejections were NOT in compliance or if 'none of the above' is checked for the characteristics, this question will not be available. When available, check 'Yes' if the rejection(s) meet the criteria for an accolade as established; consult current accolade procedures and guidance documents. If Yes, complete the required sentence per accolade procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP — Basis for rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Nonstatutory Double Patenting, check basis for rejection(s): a. Provisional b. Nonprovisional
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether the basis relied on for the Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection is provisional or nonprovisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP — Type of rejection (anticipatory or obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of rejection (check all that apply): a. Anticipatory Type b. Obviousness Type
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether the nonstatutory double patenting rejection is based on an anticipation-type analysis or an obviousness-type analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Were all Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection(s) in compliance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection(s) in compliance? Yes or No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection was made in the Office action being reviewed, the answer must be updated to either Yes or No. The determination of compliance is based on the rejection properly identifying the claim(s) and being supported by sufficient evidence. Consult statutory compliance standard and scenarios. If 'Yes' go to question 7; if 'No' continue to question 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claim(s) with non-compliant Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim discussed individually as a basis for the noncompliance in an 'Explanation of Noncompliance' section in addition to those dependent claims which inherit the noncompliance must be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in (check only one): a. Only the independent claim(s) b. Only the dependent claim(s) c. Both the independent claim(s) and dependent claim(s). This identifies the root of noncompliance in the claim tree; examples illustrate choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: For nonstatutory noncompliant claims, was another compliant Nonstatutory DP rejection applied?
rubrics_metrics.description: For all claims identified as noncompliant, was another compliant Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection applied? Yes or No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual claim may be rejected under Nonstatutory Double Patenting under multiple bases with one basis being compliant while others are not compliant. If every claim listed as noncompliant has another compliant basis, answer 'Yes'. If even one does not, answer 'No'. Consult MRF In-part Instruction document for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP Noncompliance reason — Failure to identify claims/statute (6a)
rubrics_metrics.description: 6(a): The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or correct basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When either the claim(s) or the statute is the basis of the noncompliance, this box should be checked. Do not use this box to capture failures of evidentiary support (use 6(c)). If the examiner improperly made the rejection provisional instead of non-provisional (or vice versa), check 6(a). Do not check when the reviewer believes the rejection should have been made under 35 U.S.C. 101 Statutory Double Patenting (raise as omitted 101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP Noncompliance reason — should have been statutory 101 (6b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 6(b): The rejection(s) should have been made under 35 U.S.C. 101 Statutory Double Patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the reviewer believes the proper basis is statutory 101 rather than nonstatutory DP; this may be raised as an omitted 101 Statutory Double Patenting issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP Noncompliance reason — insufficient evidence (6c) with five sub-items
rubrics_metrics.description: 6(c): The rejection(s) does not provide sufficient evidence to support that the claimed invention is not patentably distinct. If checked, identify basis by selecting at least one of 6ci-6cv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subitems: i. improperly relied on anticipation when should have relied on obviousness; ii. improperly relied on obviousness when should have relied on anticipation; iii. improperly concluded not patentably distinct without either anticipation or obviousness analysis (absent any claim matching/analysis); iv. improperly relied on the instant specification as basis; v. Other. Provide explanation consistent with boxes checked; avoid rhetorical questioning and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP Additional Info/Feedback — noncompliance due to unreasonable claim interpretation (7a)
rubrics_metrics.description: 7a: The noncompliance is the result of an unreasonable claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 7a when the basis for noncompliance is based on a limitation which was improperly construed and/or given patent significance. Only check when the rejection provides some guidance or indication of how the claim limitation is being construed so as to read on the prior art; do not check when the interpretation cannot be determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP Comments field (best practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstatutory Double Patenting Rejection(s) Comments (suggestions, feedback, best practices, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments here should not be directed to any basis of noncompliance. The reviewer may include suggestions or feedback to benefit the examiner; noncompliance explanations should be in the appropriate comment box under Question 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory Double Patenting rejection(s) — limited claim lumping
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) addresses substantially all claims individually and only groups claims together that are of substantially similar scope (i.e. limited claim lumping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check characteristics that apply. 'Substantially' and 'reasonably' permit reviewer judgment; checking indicates presence of characteristic, not accolade-worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory DP — reasonably pinpoints where limitations are met
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) reasonably pinpoints where substantially all limitations are met by the conflicting claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection reasonably identifies where claim limitations map to the conflicting claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory DP — articulates reasonable rationale for modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) articulates a reasonable rationale for each modification individually addressing each modification with a separate rationale as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the office action provides separate, reasonable rationales for each proposed modification used to reach the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory DP — patentable weight statements included
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of patentable weight are included, particularly when patentable weight is not being given to Intended use limitations, Preamble, or Claim language that suggests or makes optional some structure or steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate presence of statements discussing patentable weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory DP — claim interpretation stated
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) sets forth a claim interpretation that points out how the examiner is interpreting the claim/term/phrase for purposes of the rejection(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the office action indicates the claim interpretation used (e.g., BRI, special definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory DP — detailed legal analysis included
rubrics_metrics.description: Included detailed legal analysis of applicable legal issues through a detailed analysis of the claim(s) and the case law/policy that applies thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when detailed legal analysis is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory DP — detailed technical analysis included
rubrics_metrics.description: Included detailed technical analysis in regards to the invention and/or the conflicting claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when technical analysis is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Nonstatutory DP — included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s) (not general FP language or indication of claims with allowable subject matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when concrete suggestions to overcome the rejection are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory DP — none of the above characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check if none of the listed characteristics are exemplified in the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accolade for Nonstatutory DP rejections available?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to Non-Statutory Double Patenting Rejection(s)? Yes or No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any Nonstatutory DP rejections were NOT in compliance or if 'none of the above' is checked for characteristics, this question will not be available. When available, check 'Yes' if the rejection(s) meet accolade criteria and complete the required sentence per current accolade procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other rejections — were all 'Other' rejection(s) in compliance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 'Other' rejection(s) in compliance? Yes or No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rejection was made that is not otherwise covered in the MRF, update answer to Yes or No. Determination based on rejection properly identifying the claim(s), the statute (including subparagraphs) and being supported by sufficient evidence to support the conclusion of obviousness. Consult statutory compliance standard and scenarios. If 'No', select one of: Attention Needed or Noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claim(s) with non-compliant 'Other' rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim discussed individually as a basis for the noncompliance in an 'Explanation of Noncompliance' section in addition to those dependent claims which inherit the noncompliance must be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in (check only one): a. Only the independent claim(s); b. Only the dependent claim(s); c. Both the independent claim(s) and dependent claim(s). Examples illustrate selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of 'Other' Noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer should explain the basis for the noncompliance related to the identification of the claim(s) and/or statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The write up should avoid rhetorical questioning and not be personalized; it should be an assessment of the work product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Rejection(s) Comments (suggestions, feedback, best practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments for 'Other' rejections: suggestions, feedback, best practices etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments here should not be directed to any basis of a noncompliance; those issues should be provided in Question 3. Comments on best practices are optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted rejections — general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The allowance (or non-rejection) of a claim is statutorily compliant as long as the Office did not omit a statutorily compliant rejection. A proposed omitted rejection can be made when a claim: a) was indicated as allowed or allowable; or b) was not rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rejection made is easily overcome (e.g. swear behind, invoking exceptions under 35 USC 102(b)(1) or 102(b)(2)), the reviewer should not propose an omitted rejection but may propose a back-up rejection for TC consideration. See question 45 of MRG Guidance for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection 35 U.S.C. 102 standard (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102 when the invention is anticipated (or is 'not novel') over a disclosure that is available as prior art. To reject a claim as anticipated by a reference, the disclosure must teach every element required by the claim under its broadest reasonable interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard reviewers must apply when proposing an omitted 102 rejection. The omitted rejection must identify claims for which an omitted 102 rejection is proposed and provide a thorough description of the omitted rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted 102 — identify claims and whether directed to independent/dependent/both
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the claim(s) where a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 was omitted and indicate if the omitted rejection(s) is directed to Only the independent claim(s), Only the dependent claim(s), or Both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim proposed for an omitted 102 rejection. Do not list claims that have a compliant rejection even if covered by the omitted rejection. Each claim listed must be specifically addressed in the 'Give a thorough description' box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted 102 — identify references relied on in the omitted rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete for each reference applied in an omitted 102 rejection: Name, Document Identifier, US(F) CPC Classification Symbol, Found by, Reference Type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting 'Found by', if the reference is of record (892 or 1449) those should be selected. If found by Reviewer Search or Other, provide the search string or detailed explanation of how/where the reference was located. Follow MPEP 707.05(e) for NPL bibliographic info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted 102 — give a thorough description of the omitted rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposed rejection for each claim listed must be provided. For each claim, the statute, subparagraph and evidence supporting the rejection must be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rejection should not be personalized and should reflect a thorough analysis of how the prior art applied anticipates the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection 35 U.S.C. 103 standard (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 when the invention is obvious subject matter. To support the conclusion that the claimed invention should have been rejected as directed to obvious subject matter, the proposed rejection should articulate a prima facie case of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of fact should be supported by sufficient evidence in the prior art. The rejection should articulate how the prior art is to be modified to arrive at the claimed invention. The reasoning/rationale should be taught by the prior art applied or provided by the reviewer in a convincing line of reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted 103 — identify claims and whether directed to independent/dependent/both
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the claim(s) where a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 was omitted and indicate if the omitted rejection(s) is directed to Only the independent claim(s), Only the dependent claim(s), or Both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted 103 rejection is proposed; do not list claims that have a compliant rejection even if covered by the omitted rejection. Each claim listed must be specifically addressed in the 'Give a thorough description' box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted 103 — identify references relied on in the omitted rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete for each reference applied in an omitted 103 rejection: Name, Document Identifier, US(F) CPC Classification Symbol, Found by, Reference Type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting 'Found by', if the reference is of record (892 or 1449) those should be selected. For references found by Reviewer Search or Other, provide search strings or detailed explanation of location. Provide required bibliographic and classification info for patent documents; see MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted 103 — give a thorough description of the omitted rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposed omission for each claim must identify statute/subparagraph, evidence, and articulate a prima facie case of obviousness with supporting findings of fact and rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how prior art would be modified to arrive at the claimed invention; provide convincing line of reasoning taught by or based on prior art. The proposed rejection should not be personalized.
